text: Stavros' hard constraint for the managed-volumes work: losing user data is unacceptable under any circumstance, no exceptions. This is why the volume code only ever deletes Docker's volume *records* (bookkeeping) and never volume contents, why ownership is proven by our own com.harbormaster.app label rather than inferred from a volume's shape, and why any Docker failure during stale-app cleanup skips that app's filesystem work rather than pressing on. When touching this area, prefer refusing to act over acting on an uncertain inference.

Rejected for managed volumes: emitting the volume definitions into a separate Compose override file passed with an extra -f, instead of rewriting the app's own Compose file. It is cleaner code and sidesteps YAML rewriting entirely, but Stavros wants the checked-out Compose file to stay self-contained so that a plain 'docker compose logs' or 'docker compose up' in the repo directory behaves identically to what Harbormaster runs. Avoiding that awkwardness was the original motivation for the whole feature (the  approach forces you to set environment variables before any manual Compose command), so an override file would have reintroduced the problem in a new form. Also rejected: persisting per-app state recording which apps ever enabled manage_volumes, proposed so stale-app cleanup could skip Docker entirely for legacy apps. Judged unnecessary complexity; the failure type is enough to decide.

The gitchangelog pre-commit hook was removed rather than repaired, and it should not be re-added in that shape. Two reasons, neither reconstructable now that the config is deleted. First, the entry was 'bash -c "gitchangelog > CHANGELOG.md"', so the shell truncated CHANGELOG.md before gitchangelog even started; when gitchangelog failed the file was left at zero bytes, and it destroyed an unreleased changelog entry once. Second, it ran at commit stage, where the commit being made is not yet in git history, so the file it wrote was permanently one commit behind. Fixing it via additional_dependencies was considered and does not work either: the hook was 'language: system', for which pre-commit ignores additional_dependencies. CHANGELOG.md is now maintained by hand between releases. The GitLab release job still generates a changelog independently, installing its own gitchangelog from PyPI and reading .gitchangelog.rc, which is why that rc file was kept.

Stavros intends to adopt release-please for changelog and release management eventually (stated 2026-08-14, when the gitchangelog pre-commit hook was removed). This has not been done and there is no ticket for it yet. If changelog automation comes up again, prefer moving to release-please over reviving gitchangelog.
